details: The United States and Iran have reportedly agreed to de-escalate recent hostilities following an exchange of strikes in and around the Strait of Hormuz. A U.S. official stated that vessels should now be able to move freely through the key waterway. However, there are conflicting reports regarding the immediate resumption of technical talks, with an Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister denying scheduled meetings, even as President Trump indicated a meeting in Qatar. This fragile situation contributes to market caution.
title: US and Iran Agree to Stand Down, Talks Remain Uncertain Over Strait of Hormuz

details: The European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation is set to become fully enforceable on July 1, 2026. This landmark regulation requires crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) operating in the EU to be licensed. Estimates suggest that a significant number of existing crypto platforms (potentially over 75%) currently serving European users may not yet have the necessary authorization and will be forced to cease operations or transition clients to compliant entities. This will reshape the European crypto market.
title: EU's MiCA Crypto Regulation Fully Enforceable July 1, Thousands of Platforms Affected

details: U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have experienced substantial capital outflows in June 2026, reaching approximately $4.3 billion, marking the worst month for these products since their launch. This sustained institutional selling, now entering its eighth consecutive week, has put significant downward pressure on Bitcoin's price, which remains near its weakest levels for the year. This trend is exacerbated by a hawkish stance from the U.S. Federal Reserve, raising expectations for continued tight monetary policy.
title: Bitcoin ETFs Face Record $4.3 Billion Outflows in June, Market Under Pressure
